messages:
maria: Heads up — noticed a p99 spike after enabling the adaptive coalesce jitter on the canary cluster. p50 stable, p99 up ~12ms. Kernel selection also flipped more often to grouped_matmul. Any quick ideas?

ashok: Saw that too. Early look: KV cache miss rate increased during the canary ramp (98% -> ~94%). Flamegraph from perf-bot shows extra time in kv::lookup and queue wait. Could be head-of-line blocking from widened windows. :thinking_face:

devon: Can you paste the exact canary window config? want to see microbatch vs coalesce delay and jitter params.

maria: Config we rolled: 
```
{
  "microbatch_interval_ms": "2",
  "coalesce_delay_ms": "1",
  "jitter_strategy": "asymmetric_adaptive",
  "jitter_sigma_ms": "0.8",
  "token_budget_softcap": "128"
}
```

sam: My quick thought: asymmetric_adaptive + sigma=0.8 on tails will bunch arrivals for some routes. Try lowering sigma to 0.3 or adding queue-depth hysteresis (disable jitter when queue_depth > 8). That avoids piling on during brief floods.

kv-watchdog: Observed KV priming drop at canary start: primed_hits 98% -> 92% for the first minute of traffic. That correlates with increased lookup latency and p99. Short priming window may help. Also note some keys age out faster with the current expiry heuristics.

devon: Also a kernel note: runtime prefers grouped_matmul when effective window > 2ms; on h100 that kernel gives higher variance for tiny batches (1-3) — switching to small-batched kernel when batch_size < 4 reduces p99 at cost of minor throughput loss.

maria: Plan proposal: run 3 quick canary arms A/B/C across same host pool: 
A) no jitter (baseline)
B) fixed small jitter (0.5ms)
C) asymmetric_adaptive sigma=0.3 + queue-hysteresis (disable jitter if queue_depth>8) + priming warmup 15s
Each arm 30m, collect p50/p95/p99, kv_miss_rate, kernel_choice_ratio, token_budget utilization. Also include token_budget sweep [64,96,128] in the arms.

ashok: +1 to plan. include airflow to sample per-route histograms. Also record arrival_histogram so we can try arrival-driven jitter next.

perf-bot: scheduled canaries: canary_group=asym-jitter-scan, duration=30m per arm, metrics=[p50,p95,p99,kv_miss,kernel_ratio,token_util]; start_ts=3167894400

deploy-bot: canary started at 3167894400 (group: asym-jitter-scan). Reporting back in ~90m. :rocket:

maria: Initial metrics after first 10m of arm C: p99 baseline=48ms -> C=60ms, kv_miss +3.2pp, grouped_kernel ratio 22% -> 59%. p95 bump ~6ms.

devon: That grouped_kernel shift is suspicious. If jitter makes more arrivals align, we get more medium windows which trigger grouped kernel auto-selection. Quick mitigation: alter kernel selector to prefer small-batched kernel if batch_size distribution has >40% batches <=3. We can implement a soft threshold in selector.

sam: I can prototype selector flag: `prefer_small_when_small_pct=0.4` and `selector_lookback_ms=500`. Will submit a tiny PR to runtime.

maria: Also trying a micro change: reduce microbatch_interval_ms -> 1ms for a subset to see if smaller window prevents grouped kernel flip. Running mini-canary now on 2 hosts.

perf-bot: mini-canary (microbatch_interval_ms=1) results: p99 improved ~5ms compared to arm C, but throughput fell ~1.8%. KV_miss unchanged.

ashok: So tradeoff: smaller microbatch reduces kernel flip but slightly loses throughput. If we combine smaller microbatch + jitter_sigma 0.3 + priming warmup, might hit p99 budget.

kv-watchdog: Priming warmup helps: prefetching top-20 prefixes for active routes reduced initial miss spike to ~95% primed_hits. worth adding to rollout.

devon: Long-term: consider decoupling kernel selection signal from raw window size and instead use observed batch_size distribution + backlog tail index. That prevents jitter-driven window changes from flipping kernels.

maria: Agreed. Short-term actions:
- Run full 3-arm canary with token_budget sweep (A/B/C) but use microbatch_interval=1ms for arm C candidate.
- Sam to open PR for selector soft threshold.
- Add priming warmup (15s) to rollout recipe.
- Add queue-hysteresis rule to jitter controller.
I'll collate metrics after the canary and open an RFC if results mixed.

sam: PR #3482 coming in this afternoon for selector flag. I'll include unit tests and a small perf patch.

perf-bot: canary run scheduled finish at 3167896200. Aggregated report will be posted to the thread with flamegraphs and kernel ratio table.

maria: Thanks all — putting the follow-ups into a short checkpoint doc. If anyone wants to join the postmortem deep-dive, ping me. :eyes:
